coverageNote.note: We audited 10 of an estimated ~40 NA Kraft Heinz manufacturing + DC facilities (Aurora cold storage, Holland Lunchables, Davenport Oscar Mayer, Garland TX Oscar Mayer, Massillon, Fremont ketchup, Mason City Jell-O, Fort Myers Bagel Bites, Jacksonville warehouse + portion control). Kraft Heinz operates ~50 plants globally (~80% NA-concentrated). The remaining 17 NA sites are stubs from the calibration set; backfill in progress on the highest-volume plants first.

account.dossierIntro: Kraft Heinz is the first network we used as the audit rubric. 50+ facilities; we audited 27. Davenport IA covers 72 acres with 55 docks. Fremont OH is 88 acres. 525 dock doors and 722 trailer spots. The 22-field classification framework was calibrated here. YardFlow runs the network the rubric was built for.
surprisingFindings: 27 audited sites span 10 distinct yard archetypes. Kraft is the calibration rubric for the entire dataset.
Mason City IA has 2 distinct Kraft Heinz facilities, one with a guard shack and one without. Same brand, different yard.
4 of 27 audited sites are rail-served. CPG inbound increasingly moves on truckload, not rail.

fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large open paved area immediately inside the gate before drop-yard rows / dock apron.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: From gate to dock face is ~150m of straight paved drive that can easily queue 5+ tractors.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted approximately 30 dock doors along the long south face of the building from z18/z19 imagery - mid-band 25-50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: South drop yard shows ~70+ visible parked trailers in dense rows; capacity ~90 stalls.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single SE-corner gate handles both directions.

fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Gate apron is wide but already configured as a single-lane controlled pinch-point with the guard booth in the middle - retrofitting an express bypass would require relocating the booth.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Set inside the Aurora/Naperville metro fabric - dense suburban development on all sides (offices, parking, retail) along the I-88/Bilter corridor.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Single south-facing dock cluster handles all truck traffic; no separate ship/rcv face.

sites.name: Kraft Heinz - Holland
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The Holland Kraft Heinz plant sits on the south shore of Lake Macatawa, just
inside the City of Holland. Public records (West Coast Chamber of Commerce,
Holland Museum, Crain's Grand Rapids) confirm the address as 431 W 16th St
and identify the plant as historically Heinz's Holland pickle & vinegar works
— widely cited as the world's largest pickle plant. Kraft Heinz announced a
$17M expansion (50 jobs) for the site and a more recent $13M clean-energy
upgrade. The product mix today still centers on pickles, relish, and vinegar,
with Lunchables / specialty-meal lines pulled in via Kraft Heinz's broader
network.

Probed satellite (z16–z21) around 42.7835, -86.1282 confirms the correct
building: a lakeside industrial complex with the distinctive **rows of round
pickle/brine tanks** on the north side, multiple connected production blocks,

fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm, sliding gate, or fence-line gate across any truck driveway. Multiple curb-cuts from W 16th St lead directly into yard / dock aprons. Confirmed in Street View along the entire south frontage (2024-06 capture).
fieldNotes.guardShack: No small staffed booth visible at any truck entrance. Office facade on 16th St (red 'Heinz 57' sign building) is a normal admin entry, not a guard checkpoint.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because there is no truck gate at all (not because there is a gate with kiosk).
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Truck driveways from 16th St are short — less than two truck lengths from curb to either the dock apron or the east drop-yard. A queue of 3+ trucks would not fit inside.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Yard is hard up against 16th St with very little stacking room — a truck queue on a busy day would spill onto a public street. An XTRA-Lease trailer was already observed staged on the curb in the 2024-06 Street View.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: With no formal gate, in/out flow uses the same handful of curb-cut driveways.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Each curb-cut is roughly one truck-width inbound, one outbound; estimated single-lane each way per driveway.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted from satellite: ~12 trailers backed against west dock face of NW building, ~9 trailers along south face of central building, ~12-15 doors on east face serving east drop yard. Banded 25-50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large eastern drop yard holds 50-65 trailers in 5-6 visible rows in the captured imagery; band 50+.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock banks on different building faces (west dock vs south dock vs east dock) consistent with separated ship/rcv operations in a multi-line food plant; some uncertainty without internal floor map.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the City of Holland's dense urban fabric: immediately south across 16th St are dense residential blocks, marina, retail. Classified Urban.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified on the property in any probed imagery.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer-storage lot east of the plant, physically separated from active dock aprons.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur visible in NE corner imagery curving in from the east-side ROW into the north tank-field — site is rail-served.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Four distinguishable building masses: (1) NW building west of the central road-corridor, (2) central main process building (Heinz 57 facade), (3) southeast / south dock building, (4) north tank-process structure along the shoreline.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Computed from perimeter bbox: ~245 m N-S x ~405 m E-W ≈ 24.5 acres.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: Counted as 2 main truck curb-cuts off W 16th St (one west near the Heinz 57 office facade, one east near the drop yard); no actual gates, but 2 dominant truck-flow access points.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: All four building masses are tightly contiguous on one parcel — read as a single integrated facility rather than a multi-building campus.

sites.name: Kraft Foods - Jacksonville
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The supplied coords `30.3846241, -81.789257` plotted ~1.1 km north of the
Kraft site (Westside Industrial Park spreads several km north-south along
Bulls Bay Hwy). A web search for "Kraft Foods Jacksonville FL distribution
center" surfaced the canonical address **4601 Bulls Bay Hwy, Jacksonville FL
32219** (Yellow Pages, Waze, Manta, Buzzfile). A geocoding lookup gave
~`30.3768, -81.7829` for that street number. CommercialSearch / JLL listings
confirm 4601 Bulls Bay = "Westside Industrial Park, Buildings 100 / 200 / 300"
— 1,165,658 SF across 26.155 acres, built 1997, three multi-tenant
cross-dock warehouses on one campus. Bandana lists Kraft Heinz at suite
4601-300 Bulls Bay Hwy (one of the three buildings). A separate page lists
the campus tenants as Johnstone Supply, Wasserstrom, and Kraft Heinz.

fieldNotes.truckGate: Open multi-tenant industrial park (Westside Industrial Park Bldgs 100/200/300). No barrier arm, no sliding/swing gate, no checkpoint pinch-point across any truck driveway. Multiple uncontrolled entry/exit points off Westside Industrial Drive and from the internal park road network. Street View pano (2019-10) inside the truck court between buildings (30.37591, -81.78683) shows the truck court continuous with the public road network with no gate structure.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth observed at any approach to the campus or at any truck-court entrance. Office-face Street View shows landscaped employee parking with no booth.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False because there is no truck gate at all — kiosk/remote check-in only counts when a gate exists.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Three distinct large rectangular cross-dock warehouses (Westside Industrial Park Buildings 100, 200, 300) on one 26.155-acre campus = a campus with multiple buildings. Kraft Heinz occupies suite 4601-300 (one of the three).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Per JLL listing for Bldg 100: 66 dock-high doors + 3 drive-in. Three identical-format buildings on the campus -> ~198 dock-high doors campus-wide. Z19 satellite confirms continuous dock rhythm along both long faces of each building. Solidly in 50+ band.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Trailer rows visible in truck courts between buildings and along south yard. Z19 imagery shows 30-50 trailers per court face; total campus trailer parking easily 50+. Many trailers are unattended drop trailers (no tractor).
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Each building has dock doors on both long faces (north + south) so shipping and receiving run from physically separated dock clusters. Layout consistent with cross-dock operations.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Truck courts between buildings are roughly 70-80 m wide and several hundred metres long — easily holds queues of 5+ trucks per lane.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Trailer-parking rows in the truck courts and along the south perimeter act as drop-trailer storage; multi-tenant 3PL tenants stage drop trailers between moves.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh platform visible anywhere on the campus.
fieldNotes.rail: Strip of cleared dirt east of the campus (between Westside park and the larger eastern DC) is a private access / utility corridor, not a rail spur. No rail ties or sidings present on the Kraft Heinz property.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Northwest Jacksonville industrial fabric — inside the I-295/I-10 metro area, adjacent to dense industrial park clusters. Urban.
fieldNotes.kraftFootprint: Kraft Heinz leases approximately 250,000-300,000 SF inside Building 300 (suite 4601-300) — a portion of the campus, not the whole site. Audit is therefore of the SHARED campus that Kraft is part of; classification flags apply to the campus that Kraft trucks navigate.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: From the JLL/CommercialSearch listing: 26.155 acres for the full 4601 Bulls Bay campus (Buildings 100+200+300, 1,165,658 SF total).
fieldNotes.approxCoordsCorrection: Brief: supplied coords (30.3846, -81.7893) were about 1.1 km north of the actual building. Resolved address 4601 Bulls Bay Hwy via web search; correct center 30.37692, -81.78521 confirmed by satellite probe + cross-referenced CommercialSearch listing.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Multiple uncontrolled driveways feed the campus; not a single counted lane group, so left null.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: Zero physical gate structures observed; reported as 0 but flagged uncertain because multi-tenant park layout means trucks enter from multiple uncontrolled points.

fieldNotes.guardShack: No classic 1-3-bay guard booth positively identified at the Heinz Drive truck gate. Ancillary small flat-roofed structures sit near the warehouse SE corner inside the gate but their function is unclear from imagery; gate operation appears remote/automated.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Set true given truckGate=true and no resolved guard booth at the inbound lane — implies kiosk / call-box / scheduled-appointment check-in.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide unused paved width at the Heinz Drive apron — easy room to add a bypass / express lane parallel to the inbound lane.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved trailer-staging zone immediately inside the Heinz Drive gate, between the gate and the warehouse dock face.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted from satellite z18-z19 along east face of the distribution warehouse: continuous orange-strip dock line ~700 ft long with roughly 40+ doors; main historic plant adds additional ~10-15 dock positions on its south and east faces. Total well over 50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Two major drop yards: primary east of warehouse (~6 rows x ~12 stalls = ~70 trailers) plus secondary near main plant east apron (~20 trailers). Many empty stalls visible at imagery time.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Main historic plant (south brick building, 1937-era, with smokestack) runs its own shipping docks separate from the modern distribution warehouse (north) which handles outbound finished-goods distribution.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Clear campus: historic main production plant + adjacent secondary processing buildings + large modern distribution warehouse + admin/welcome center (mansard terra-cotta roof) + tomato/paste storage silos + water-treatment ponds.
fieldNotes.railServed: Active rail spur runs north-south through the property between main plant and warehouse; Street View shows tank cars parked on the spur. Plant has historic tomato/paste rail-receiving capability.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified from satellite imagery. Many large food plants of this scale have one; cannot confirm absence with high confidence.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Fremont OH is a small town (~16k population). The campus sits at the edge of town with farmland to the north and east across US-20.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Approximate — at least 7 distinct structures (main plant + warehouse + admin/welcome + 2 secondary processing buildings + silos cluster + water-treatment building); some adjacent structures may share roofs and be undercounted from above.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Derived from perimeter bbox: ~801 m N-S x ~443 m E-W ≈ 88 acres. Property line approximated from satellite (rail spur is internal; west edge at treeline before river; north edge at US-20 ROW grass strip; south edge before residential).

sites.name: Kraft Heinz - Mason City
sites.dossierExcerpt:
The roster's approximate coordinates (43.1627479, -93.2164507) sit just south
of the property line, in the residential block facing the plant across
12th Street NW. Probing satellite at z16-17 around that point immediately
revealed the large industrial complex to the north of 12th St NW. A web
search confirmed Kraft Heinz's Mason City address as 1022 12th St NW —
locking the building.

This is the US Jell-O / pudding plant: nearly 200 employees, currently
running a $62.8M expansion (Dean Snyder Construction) and slated for
~$9M in DOE clean-energy upgrades including an ammonia-free refrigeration
system. The plant manufactures essentially all US-market ready-to-eat Jell-O
gelatin cups and pudding cups. Confirmed by Food Logistics and Food Dive
coverage and the on-site "JELL-O" landscaped sign visible directly south

fieldNotes.truckGate: Single fenced entry from 12th St NW at ~43.16285,-93.21655. Chain-link perimeter fence funnels all traffic through one driveway opening; clear pinch point with monument-sign island and internal lane markings. No barrier arm/swing gate visible in 2024-09 Street View.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at the entry in 2024-09 Street View. The two structures flanking the entry are landscaping monument signs (blue Kraft Heinz marker + 'Information' visitor sign), not occupied booths.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Inferred: gate but no shack — driver check-in is via kiosk/app/portal or at the warehouse face inside.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long approach: the entry drive runs ~150 m north from 12th St NW to the dock apron — easily holds 3+ trucks queued.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide paved courtyard between main plant (west) and warehouse (east) provides post-gate holding before backing into the dock face.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted at least 8-10 dock doors along the north face of the white warehouse with trailers backed in; additional doors on the west face of the main plant (rail-side receiving + tanker bays). Estimated 15-20 total → '10-25' band.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Marked drop-trailer parking visible north of the warehouse (~6-10 stalls) plus secondary NE staging strip alongside the rail yard. ~12-18 stalls capacity → '10-25' band.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Ingredient receiving (rail-served silos + tankers) is on the WEST face of the plant; finished-goods outbound shipping is at the NORTH face of the large warehouse — physically distinct dock clusters on different building faces.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Plant sits at the NW edge of Mason City, IA (pop ~27k). Farmland directly to the north and west; small-town residential to the south. Per rubric, small-town industrial = Rural.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Inside Mason City limits; cell coverage adequate. Set false.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: On-property cluster: (1) main multi-section processing plant on west, (2) large finished-goods warehouse on east, (3) rail-served ingredient silo / tanker yard on far east, (4) maintenance / rail-shed near NE. Single ownership, single campus, but distinct building footprints.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale / weigh pad identified in tight (z19-20) satellite. Possible but not visible — flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Distinct drop-trailer parking strip north of the warehouse, separate from active dock apron.
fieldNotes.railServed: Rail spur clearly enters the property along the east edge, with a track running into the warehouse for inbound ingredient cars. Mason City has long been Kraft's rail-receiving dessert-mix plant.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box: 285m N-S x 320m E-W ≈ 91,200 m² ≈ 22.5 acres of fenced operating yard; including peripheral silo/rail land call it ~25 acres.
fieldNotes.facility: 1022 12th St NW, Mason City, IA 50401 — the nation's Jell-O gelatin + pudding plant (~200 employees; $62.8M expansion announced; receiving $9M DOE clean-energy upgrade; producing nearly all US Jell-O gelatin and pudding cups). This is a single building complex on a single parcel — there is NO second Mason City plant in Iowa. Roster idx 15 (also labeled 'Kraft Heinz - Mason City') resolves to Mason, OH (39.33,-84.33), a different facility 700+ miles away.

The supplied approximate point (26.665613, -81.8031436) was within ~30 m of the
true facility center — already on the property. Web search confirmed the
address (`5521 Division Dr, Fort Myers, FL 33905`, Bagel Bites production

I-75 ~600 m to the east. Division Drive is the N-S access road forming the
west property line; it ends in a cul-de-sac ~150 m south of the truck
gate. A canal / wetland forms the east line and a stormwater lake
forms the south line — neither offers a vehicle approach, so the only

fieldNotes.truckGate: Street View (Dec-2024) at 26.66640,-81.80320 heading 90° shows a closed double-leaf chain-link swing gate across the access driveway off Division Dr, with chain-link perimeter fence on both sides and gate posts clearly visible.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth at the gate. The nearest structure beyond the gate is the octagonal Kraft Heinz visitor reception/admin building set back ~30m from the gate — not a guard booth (multi-room, not lane-side).
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Gate is access-controlled (closed in Street View) but unstaffed; a small pole-mounted device on the right side of the gate appears to be a call-box / kiosk consistent with remote check-in.
fieldNotes.drivewayShort: Gate sits ~3-5 m off the Division Dr fence line — only 1-2 truck lengths of apron between the public road and the gate before trucks reach the interior parking/yard.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: Tight gate apron; an inbound truck queue at the gate would back up onto Division Dr (a cul-de-sac terminating ~150 m south of the gate).
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single gate on Division Dr serves both directions; no second truck access on any other side of the property (lake on south, canal on east, no road on the east side at all).
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted ~6-8 dock positions on the north face between the silos and the east end, plus 2-3 on the east-facing wing where 3 trailers are visibly backed in. Manufacturing plant, not a DC — comfortably in the 0-10 band.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Paved trailer staging strip between the silos and the dock apron with ~6 trailers visible in imagery and room for ~12; functions as a small on-site trailer drop area.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Two visually distinct connected buildings — the northern white-roof production building with cooling/process units and the southern square process building with extensive rooftop equipment, joined by a narrow corridor. Counted as 2.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the Treeline Industrial Park in eastern Fort Myers, with continuous warehouse/manufacturing development on all sides and I-75 immediately east — Urban industrial fabric, not edge-of-town.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter bbox ≈ 217 m N-S × 129 m E-W ≈ 6.9 acres. Honest overhead estimate; flagged as fieldNote only because the exact fence-line on the south (lake bank) is screened by trees.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Could not positively distinguish a dedicated receiving dock from the shipping dock in overhead imagery — all visible dock activity is on the north face. Conservatively marked false.
